title: A call from a family member asking urgently for money
lede: Your daughter, your son, your mother — the voice is right. They are in trouble: an accident, an arrest, a phone lost abroad, a hospital. They need money now and they cannot talk long.

blocks.text: Your daughter, your son, your mother — the voice is right. They are in trouble: an accident, an arrest, a phone lost abroad, a hospital. They need money now and they cannot talk long.

items: Voices can now be cloned convincingly from a few seconds of public audio. The voice sounding right is no longer evidence of anything.
The script always contains the same three elements: distress, urgency, and a reason you cannot verify — new number, broken phone, cannot talk, do not tell dad.
Distress bypasses verification. Parents and grandparents are targeted precisely because love makes deliberation feel like betrayal.
The payment method is the tell: transfer to a new account, crypto, vouchers, or a courier collecting cash. Real emergencies do not need these.

items.move: Hang up and call them on their known number
items.detail: The number in your phone, not the one that called you. This single step defeats nearly every version of this scam.

items.move: Ask a question no clone can answer
items.detail: Not a birthday — something only they would know: what we called the old car, what happened at the caravan. Agree such a phrase with your family in advance.

items.move: Send no money on this call
items.detail: Whatever the story. If it is genuine, ten minutes changes nothing; if it is not, ten minutes saves everything.
Call another family member. "Do not tell anyone" exists solely to stop this call happening.

items.move: If they claim to be police, lawyer, or hospital, verify independently
items.detail: Look up the institution and ring the main switchboard. Never a number they supply.
Number, time, account details, any recording. Needed for the bank and the report.

items.say: "I am going to hang up and call you back on your usual number. If you are really in trouble, you will still be there."
"Before we go on — what did we call Grandad's dog?"
"I am going to tell your mother. If that is a problem, I know what this is."
"I do not transfer money to new accounts on a phone call. Not ever."

items: Confirming names or details they fish for. "Is that you, Sarah?" hands them the script.
Transfers, crypto, vouchers, or handing cash to a courier.
Staying on the line "so it can be sorted." Keeping you on the line is a technique.
Feeling ashamed for hesitating. Verification is love, not doubt.
Agree a family code word today, out loud, with everyone. It costs one minute and it ends this entire category of attack.
If money moved, call the bank immediately and ask for a recall attempt.
Report it — these operations run at industrial scale and reports drive disruption.
Warn older relatives with the actual script, not a general warning. Specifics are what stick.

limit: Any urgent request for money, credentials, or codes that arrives by voice or video must be verified on a channel you initiate, to a number you already had. Hang up and call back. If it involved intimate imagery of you or a child, that is a criminal matter — report it, preserve the evidence, and do not negotiate with whoever sent it.
